They join livestreaming teams, collaborate with trendy works, and release more accessible songs... yet the audience clamors for more. More sorrow, more joy, more devotion, and anything else that will keep boredom at bay.

It all began with an unexpected incident: During a live show, several magical girls protected the audience from an evil imagenae, gaining an unexpectedly positive reception.
This gradually evolved into a staged spectacle: A group of magical girls, acting as villains, would interrupt the performance, only to be dramatically defeated by another group of them.
"They'll protect us, with their magical rocket launchers and magical heart lasers!" The audience's eyes sparkled with exhilaration and anticipation.

The laughter must not cease, and the joy must not falter. The girls' skirts whirl in a frenzy until the very last ounce of their strength is spent.
When the curtain falls, the crowd departs, delighted, and greedily awaiting the next spectacle of Elation.

4005353628077090723: Code: AVE-1 Date: ██████ Details: This is, without a doubt, the most intriguing commission I've taken on since becoming a detective: dig up the weakness of Aventurine, one of the Ten Stonehearts. To answer this question, this record will employ methods including, but not limited to: visual surveillance, data interception, on-site investigation, and echo recreation, all in service of building a comprehensive profile on the subject. The first stop of the investigation was the "World's End" Tavern, rumored to be a place where legends of Kakavasha still circulated. "Hey, you're literally the twentieth person asking about him this week!" Here I was expecting a tough search, but the moment I walked in, the Fools came flocking. "An Avgin? There's only one! Looked... tasty. And then. He sold me out. Darn Avgin, DARN!!!!!" The hulking brute let out a belch, pointed to the scars on his face, and slammed his fists on the table to vent his anger. "That gentleman... hehehe, well, if it weren't for him, I'd have paid off my debt long ago and wouldn't still be stuck here as a drinksmith..." The drinksmith's face was etched with bitterness. He downed a large glass and his eyes grew faintly red as the memories came flooding back. "He supposedly played a game against some big shot from the IPC once. After that, Kakavasha never showed his face in the tavern again. I've never witnessed such a breathtaking showdown in my life. His luck was like Aha THEMSELF had possessed him, and the way he played was absolutely suicidal!"① ... A Fool's story is best taken with a grain of salt. Now let's be real, a homeless Avgin street kid wandered into a tavern on a whim, and somehow managed to run circles around a bunch of Fools. Someone like that might look like they couldn't care less about anything, but given a past full of misfortune, there's bound to be some hidden wound buried deep inside, and a desire that's never been satisfied. If an ordinary gambler's thrill comes from winning, then what kind of thrill does he get from the game? The satisfaction of a perfectly laid plan? The happiness of pulling a prank? Neither. All those superficial pleasures are nothing but a carefully crafted disguise. If that weren't the case, why would he turn down the invitation of the Elation? Wouldn't becoming a Masked Fool have been the better choice? When the eyes of the entire world are drawn to his performance at the card table, I believe his hands must be trembling beneath it. My anticipation grows by the moment, Aventurine. This is no ordinary game. Let's see if I can unearth the truth you've buried so deep behind that mask. Note: ① Given the strained relationship between Aventurine and the IPC bigwig at the tavern, I once attempted to establish a working relationship with said individual, but never received a reply. — Record synced to client terminal
